title: Ghostline - Dedicated GPU isolation & quiet-hours burst discovery
summary: Intro + qualification for dedicated capacity. Talked isolation/tenant fencing, quiet-hours burst window, pre-warm vs warm-pool, KMS & VPC constraints, fallback to hosted variants, and cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed to run a synthetic burst sim and share security pack. Action: Redwood to send cost model and runbook; Customer to provide peak QPS and synthetic trace.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-19 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Marcus Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ava Reynolds (CTO - Ghostline), Samir Khan (SRE), Lena Ortiz (Product), Jon Park (Dev)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be lossy): discuss dedicated reserved GPU plan, isolation concerns for multi-tenant models, quiet-hours burst window for batch scoring, KMS integration and SOC2 questions, next step is synthetic burst run and security docs.

00:00 Marcus Liu: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro — im Marcus from Redwood, this is Priya our SE.
00:06 Ava Reynolds: hi hi, ava here, thanks for the invite. i pulled Samir and lena and jon in because they own ops and product for inference.
00:12 Priya Rao: great. i wanted to start with the high-level goals — you mentioned reserved capacity, isolation, and this quiet-hours burst pattern in your note. can you run through current infra and pain points?
00:25 Samir Khan: yeah. so today we run on a mix of on-prem gpus and some cloud endpoints. models are mostly 7b-13b with some larger 70b for nightly batch jobs. main pain is cold starts and noisy-neighbors when we run nightly re-scores. burst happens in like a 2-3 hour window at 2am local — we call that our quiet-hours surge.
00:42 Marcus Liu: okay, got it. and what SLA/latency targets do you need during those bursts vs normal day?
00:48 Lena Ortiz: for online traffic we want <180ms p95 for 7b-ish gen, for the batch window latency isn't as strict but throughput matters — we'd ideally finish re-scores within the 2-3 hour window. cost is also a factor; we cant pay for a giant warm pool all month.
01:05 Priya Rao: makes sense. a few clarifying Qs: 1) do you need absolute tenant isolation (single-tenant hardware) or logical fencing is ok? 2) any data residency / KMS rules for model input/output? 3) how spiky are the bursts — do they exceed your sustained throughput 10x, 100x?
01:20 Ava Reynolds: good questions. for HIPAA-like data (not all models) we need strict isolation for PII flows — so single-tenant or at least dedicated GPU pools for those routes. for non-PII scoring logical tenancy is ok. We use an internal KMS for keys and cannot export plaintext logs off-prem without agreement. spikes are typically 20-30x sustained for that quiet window.
01:40 Jon Park: to add, we also do canary rollouts during that period for nightly pipelines, so we need predictable capacity for both re-score and some canary tests.
01:50 Priya Rao: ok so sounds like a split approach: Dedicated pools (reserved) for PII-sensitive routes, and either Redwood-hosted dedicated or hosted fallback for non-PII. We can map that to Redwoods Dedicated + routing policies.
02:03 Marcus Liu: quick note — our Dedicated offering supports GPU pools with tenant fencing and VPC peering, plus KMS integrations. Priya will show a sketch later. before that, Samir, can you share current peak qps numbers or a synthetic trace?
02:14 Samir Khan: right now we avg 150 qps sustained; quiet-hours hits ~3k qps for short bursts (20–40 minutes of intensive job scheduling) — full re-score is about 800k items per run.
02:27 Priya Rao: that's helpful — we usually model that as 20–25x increase. for sizing we'd look at instance types, concurrency per GPU, and prewarm factors. do you currently use batching / KV cache in your runtime?
02:40 Samir Khan: we do some batching client-side but no KV cache. we also do model quantization for the 7b family — so we might want mixed-precision / int8 paths.
02:50 Marcus Liu: ok two quick tradeoffs: 1) warm pool/prewarm vs on-demand burst: warm pools give best latency but cost more ongoing. 2) prewarm windows keyed to quiet-hours can be shorter but need orchestration to spin up nodes and populate KV caches.
03:06 Ava Reynolds: on cost — what's the typical monthly hit for keeping a warm pool sized to handle 3k qps?
03:12 Priya Rao: rough numbers: depends on GPU type — e.g., an A100 class equivalent in our pool can handle X gen throughput; to support 3k qps with target latency you might need 6-10 gpus in active warm pool for the duration. we will produce a detailed cost model after we get your trace.
03:27 Jon Park (interrupt): X gen throughput — small aside — what's the overhead for switching between quantized and full-precision models? we dont want to keep two copies warmed.
03:36 Priya Rao: good point. we support model variants and our runtime can fall back to a compatible variant on capacity constraints; switching does cost KV warming and some latency spike. an approach is to pin the primary variant to dedicated and let lower-priority variants run on shared capacity.
03:50 Speaker 1: (unclear) — how do you handle preemption if host cloud reclaims nodes?
03:55 Marcus Liu: generally reserved Dedicated pools are not preemptible — that's the point. if you're on Dedicated Reserved we guarantee capacity within your SLA; if you want burst beyond reserved, we have defined burst paths: 1) your reserved pool + 2) a warm ephemeral pool (short-term commit) + 3) fallback to hosted compatible model variants with SLO guardrails.
04:14 Samir Khan: what about the quiet-hours being at 2am — our ops team sleeps then. can Redwood auto-trigger prewarm and notify?
04:22 Priya Rao: yes, you can schedule prewarm jobs — or trigger via API when your pipeline starts. we also support lifecycle hooks and webhooks for alerting.
04:30 Ava Reynolds: on compliance — we are SOC2-in-progress and need to know what logs/ audit trails Redwood will provide, plus SSO/SAML integration for RBAC.
04:40 Marcus Liu: we provide audit logs for request-level metadata, token-level cost, per-route latency, and model versioning. SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning is supported. for Dedicated Private we can arrange KMS/HSM integrations — Priya will capture the exact connectors we support.
04:55 Lena Ortiz: curious about data retention — can you redact transcripts/token logs for PII?
05:00 Priya Rao: yes, we have redaction policies and can configure token-level retention and masking. for stricter needs you can route PII workloads entirely to your private on-prem Dedicated deployment.
05:10 Jon Park: ok can we talk about failure modes? if a single GPU in the dedicated pool fails during the re-score, how does traffic shift — will the run time spill to hosted and do we get throttled?
05:21 Marcus Liu: in a failure, autoscaling and routing policies matter. we support automatic fallback: at configured thresholds we route low-priority traffic to hosted variants. You can also configure queueing/backpressure and retry policies. we do try to keep higher priority reserved routes within the Dedicated pool as long as capacity permits. you'll get alerts and a tracing link.
05:43 Priya Rao: one more nuance — if you need single-tenant physical isolation, we provision isolated GPU nodes (no multi-tenant colocations). that can be more expensive but meets strict compliance.
05:55 Samir Khan: that's what our security team will ask for. what's the typical provisioning lead time for single-tenant nodes?
06:02 Marcus Liu: depends on region and stock, but typically 2-6 weeks to provision for Dedicated Reserved single-tenant capacity; we can sometimes expedite with partner inventory. for hybrid approaches — reserved logical pools can be faster (days).
06:18 Ava Reynolds: timeline wise, we are hoping to pilot in Q1 to support a Feb re-score cadence. Is that doable?
06:25 Priya Rao: yes, if we get a signed PO for reserved capacity and we run the synthetic burst sim this month, Q1 pilot aligns. we'll need details for prewarm/scripts and security signoff.
06:34 Marcus Liu: okay i'm going to sketch the technical plan: 1) Redwood will run a synthetic burst simulation using your traces to size the reserved pool and warm-pool needs. 2) We'll propose a hybrid topology: isolated reserved pools for PII routes, shared dedicated for non-PII, warm ephemeral units for burst, fallback to hosted variants. 3) Integrate KMS via customer-managed keys, SAML for SSO, and provide audit logs.
06:52 Samir Khan: for the sim — we can send over a 48h trace and some synthetic QPS scenarios. can you also include eviction/preemption tests?
06:59 Priya Rao: yes we can simulate node failure and partial preemption to show graceful degradation. we'll include expected latency curves and cost delta.
07:10 Jon Park: what's the pricing model for the warm ephemeral units used only during quiet-hours? is that billed hourly or by minute?
07:16 Marcus Liu: we bill reserved capacity monthly (commit), warm ephemeral units can be hourly and we have a burst discount for short windows. we'll include exact numbers in the cost model.
07:26 Lena Ortiz: two more items — do you support customer-managed network peering (VPC peering) for dedicated? and can we keep token-level exec logs inside our VPC?
07:34 Priya Rao: yes for Redwood Private/Dedicated we support VPC peering and private control plane; logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint or retained per your retention policy.
07:45 Ava Reynolds: ok this is helpful. can we talk about an example failure scenario — say we hit a 50% drop in dedicated capacity mid-run — what's our expected impact on P95 latency and completion time?
07:58 Priya Rao: we'll provide an SLO degradation matrix in the sim results. rough ballpark: if capacity drops 50% and you reroute X% to hosted variants, p95 can double for some gen requests unless you accept lower quality variants. that's why warm-pool plus KV caching is often used to absorb transient loss.
08:20 Marcus Liu: any other questions?
08:24 Ava Reynolds: yes around security docs — can you send SOC2 attestation and a sandbox config for KMS?
08:30 Marcus Liu: absolutely. we'll attach the security pack and an onboarding checklist.
08:34 Action recap (auto): Redwood to run synthetic burst simulation and send cost model + security pack. Ghostline to provide trace, peak qps, and list of PII routes. Schedule pilot kick-off.

08:45 Closing and next steps recap by Marcus: 
- Redwood: run sim, share cost model, share Dedicated topology diagram, share SOC2 docs and KMS connector guide.
- Ghostline: share 48h traces, mark PII routes, internal sign-off timeline, decide pilot date.

End transcript (note: occasional mis-transcriptions present; speaker labels approximate).
